alignments.note: Jussive rendered by the volitive frame Let them melt away (rule 17); away completes the lexeme of the Niphal.
Relative supplied over an asyndetic finite clause juxtaposed to the written antecedent water (rules 46, 55).
Hithpael 'go about' rendered runneth apace as one rendering; apace stays with the verb rather than being read as the dative's.
Suffix of the ethical dative, no pronoun written for it (rule 40).
Subordinator supplied for a clause the Hebrew writes with no conjunction (rule 55).

Noun arrows; the supplied subject them of the ASV's recast clause resumes this noun, the only morpheme in the verse denoting the arrows, so it joins its discontinuous unit (rule 25). Competing reading: them added under rule 20's closing sentence. Variant WLC.PSA.58.7.v001 selected r00-base; nothing excluded.

כְּמוֹ before a finite clause rendered as though; the ASV makes it the predicate of a recast jussive clause and the frame let ... be is the construction-supplied copula with its modal (rule 49), headed on as. Competing reading: let them be as one added run.
Verb with subject pronoun and passive frame; off completes cut off (rule 44).

review_notes: Second colon is heavily recast; When, that are added, the copula frame is placed on the second כְּמוֹ, and them on arrows.
